workflow: A callback is implemented with a parameter signedness that differs from the interface type used for dispatch.
The callback is registered or invoked through the interface despite the incompatible function signature.
A call passes the argument through the mismatched function-pointer type.
Undefined-behavior instrumentation detects the incompatible indirect call and reports a runtime failure instead of completing normally.
summary: Incompatible callback parameter signedness causes instrumented indirect-call failure
decision_reason: The underlying failure workflow is materially the same as the existing cluster: a callback with an incompatible concrete signature is dispatched through a generic function-pointer interface, producing undefined behavior during an indirect call.
